title: A name at the gate
purpose: Choose identity; establish a returnee who wants to participate.
staging: Airport forecourt; player grey silhouette until identity choice; driver carries a handwritten family pickup note.
arc: Player knows the family through messages but hesitates in person.
exchanges: Welcome. I am your family’s driver today. How are you?
A long flight. Your family is waiting.
I am happy to be here.
One more time, so I have your name right. Who are you?
I am the driver. You are {player}.

title: One small journey
purpose: Offer a safe first request and introduce the return-flight limit without a countdown.
staging: Driver indicates car; suitcase changes position on success. No separate greeter sprite.
arc: Player chooses to ask rather than pretend to understand.
exchanges: Your return flight is after the wedding. A short visit.
Yes. I want to see everyone.
Are you ready? We can go now.

title: Looking together
purpose: Teach pointing through visible roadside referents.
staging: External car only. Coconut tree, church, village and sea pass in separate readable layers. Hold a landmark during each choice.
arc: Driver waits for the player’s response rather than filling every silence.
exchanges: Look. That is a coconut tree.
Look ahead. That is a church.
Look ahead. The church is there.
That is the village. We are going this way.

title: The last turn
purpose: Retrieve a landmark before arrival; close atomic onboarding.
staging: Repeat church silhouette already seen; background stops at house gate after retrieval.
arc: Player identifies something without the driver naming it first.
exchanges: Look again. That is a church.
Good. We are almost there. Your family’s house is ahead.

title: A seat is waiting
purpose: Reintroduce identity in the family setting and establish visual dress progression.
staging: Popua veranda and sitting area. Elder clears a place; player changes to repository mid-game outfit between arrival and dinner, without a dressing minigame.
arc: Elder recognises the returnee; the player need not prove belonging.
exchanges: I am your grandmother. Come and sit with me.
The wedding is soon. We are glad you came.
I am glad to be here.
This is your family. There is a place for you.
I am happy to be with my family.

title: Passing the bowl
purpose: Teach food offers, requests and family roles through a real meal.
staging: Three food props: rice, fish, taro; water jug. Items named only when visible. Final names and dishes require approval.
arc: Player can decline food politely; hospitality is never a trap.
exchanges: Are you hungry? Here is rice.
Here is fish. Here is taro.
There is more food. Would you like some?
Those two are brother and sister. They are helping too.

title: Beside the quiet cousin
purpose: Give the cousin privacy and agency without a relationship meter.
staging: Cousin sits at the table edge, phone face down only if they choose to talk; no phone confiscation.
arc: Quietness is hesitation, not a moral failure. Player admits uncertainty.
exchanges: Your cousin can show you around.
Everyone asks me to show people around.
You don’t know all the words either?
I know what they mean. Sometimes I don’t want to say them.

title: Needed for something real
purpose: Make the coordination request and contribution clear early.
staging: Relative brings a short supplies note; elder stays seated; no quest-log system.
arc: Player accepts a bounded job before knowing everything. Wedding belongs to the wider family, not solely to player success.
exchanges: We need help with the wedding. Can you help?
We need food and drinks from the market. Two bundles of food. Three drinks.
Two bundles of food. Three drinks.
Then ask the minister about the time. We will go together.
You will have a small part at the wedding, too. We will practise.
Yes. First the market. One thing at a time.

title: The right stall
purpose: Retrieve pointing and greeting before a transaction.
staging: Talamahu produce stall and adjacent drinks; at most shopkeeper, relative and optional cousin.
arc: Player begins addressing people directly instead of asking relative to speak.
exchanges: Look. That is the food stall.
Look here. Food is on this table.
Food is here. What do you need?

title: Enough for the table
purpose: Distinguish quantities from sufficiency; use simple flags instead of inventory.
staging: Shopkeeper displays two bundles and three drinks. No money arithmetic or fabricated price.
arc: Player notices a mismatch and asks for correction politely.
exchanges: The family asked for two bundles.
You asked for three. Let’s count again.

title: Ask in your own voice
purpose: Revision check without relative supplying the request; arrange payment in-world.
staging: Relative stands back. Shopkeeper hands over a single supplies prop only after the check. Payment is a handover animation, not an economy.
arc: Player can repair a small misunderstanding and still complete the errand.
exchanges: What do you need for the wedding?
I need two bundles of food and three drinks.
I need three bundles and two drinks.
Two bundles of food. Three drinks.
Good. Two bundles and three drinks.
I will pay. You asked for what we needed.

title: A little room beside you
purpose: Offer an optional cousin exchange that reconverges immediately.
staging: At stall edge; cousin may come alongside but no escort simulation.
arc: Cousin’s usefulness is acknowledged without making them responsible for player progress.
exchanges: Your cousin might come next time.
I can go with you again.
The food is ready. What did you ask for?
Two bundles of food. Three drinks.
Thank you. At the wedding, speak slowly too.

title: A different kind of hello
purpose: Introduce respectful public address in one church location.
staging: St Paul’s grounds, not a new grandma-visit branch. Minister at doorway; relative waits beside player.
arc: Player carries the conversation into a formal context.
exchanges: Here is the minister. We are here about the wedding.
Hello. We are preparing the wedding.
Hello. Welcome. How can I help?
The family is getting ready. You have come a long way.
I am happy to be with my family.
Yes. I am here to help.
Ask about the time. What time does it start?

title: Say the time back
purpose: Model and retrieve a short time confirmation.
staging: Minister indicates a single clock card showing 10:00; 10 is a proposed scheduling detail, not repository canon.
arc: Player checks information rather than nodding through uncertainty.
exchanges: The family gathering starts at ten.
At ten. We will see your family there.
We will be there at ten.
We will be there at two.
At ten. Look at the clock.
What time will we be there?

title: Whose words are these?
purpose: Bridge everyday thanks to ceremonial practice without claiming formal order.
staging: Quiet edge of same grounds; relative gives one short fragment at a time.
arc: Player asks for the contribution to sound like their own voice.
exchanges: That is enough for today. Your wedding part will be short.
First understand what you want to say. Then we will practise the words.
I want to thank my family.
I want to say I am happy to be here.
We will be there at ten.

title: An invitation without an errand
purpose: Let everyday motion language bring the cousin into their own setting.
staging: Teufaiva simplified pitch edge, one ball; no dexterity or sports scoring. Cousin is already present independent of optional earlier contact.
arc: Cousin leads here; player follows instead of recruiting them.
exchanges: You came. There is no shopping here.

title: Try again is allowed
purpose: Use repeated invitation and response as fluency practice.
staging: Ball rolls a small distance on selection; cousin retrieves it on repair. No timing inputs.
arc: Player’s imperfect attempt gives cousin permission to be imperfect.
exchanges: That went the wrong way. Try again.
You are getting better. Are you tired?
All right. One more pass, then we rest. Come.

title: Not a project to fix
purpose: Give cousin a specific fear and a modest self-directed next step.
staging: Same pitch bench; ball still. Cousin turns toward player; no forced confession.
arc: Cousin fears being corrected publicly; player offers company, not a lecture about identity.
exchanges: At home, someone always answers before I do.
Then they ask why I am quiet.
We can try one line together.
Will everyone look at you at the wedding?
You still want to do it?
I want to be part of it.
Maybe I can help you practise. Just us.

title: Tomorrow has a shape
purpose: Confirm time and supplies; change to rehearsal state in reused house.
staging: Popua evening light; bundles visible, seats arranged. Outfit remains mid-game until wedding cut.
arc: Player sees earlier choices contribute to a functioning family event.
exchanges: The supplies are here. What time tomorrow?
At ten. You checked with the minister.
Two bundles of food. Three drinks. Is that enough?
What did you ask for at the market?
I need two bundles of food and three drinks.
I need three bundles and two drinks.
Two bundles of food. Three drinks.
Tomorrow we will ask you to take your part.
I am happy to be here.

title: A voice at the same table
purpose: Give cousin a small practical rehearsal role with an opt-out.
staging: Cousin at doorway, not mandatory stage joiner. Optional extra practice branches back to core.
arc: Cousin volunteers; the player does not announce their progress to the family.
exchanges: Do you want me to stay?
If you stop, I can wait. Like you did.
We will practise one part at a time.

title: Before the room fills
purpose: Rehearse general greeting, thanks and love before path-specific sequence.
staging: Elder, relative, cousin; minimal hand or face reactions. No abstract readiness score.
arc: Player can ask for repetition while retaining dignity.
exchanges: I am happy to be with my family.

title: The work becomes a wedding
purpose: Pay off preparation with a family event already underway.
staging: Haʻatafu coastal canopy. Supplies visible; family seated. Wedding outfits follow vault; wedding couple are silent background figures, not new speaking roles.
arc: The returnee is a participant among many; no claim that a language error invalidates the marriage.
exchanges: We are here. The family is ready.
I am happy to be with my family.
There is water for the table. What do you need?
Water is here. I need water, please.
Hello, everyone. Thank you for coming.

title: After the contribution
purpose: Recognise participation without a language mastery claim.
staging: Elder nods; relative makes room beside family; cousin meets player’s eye. Return here after either successful climax only.
arc: Player receives warmth; cousin offers a sentence unprompted.
exchanges: Thank you. Come and sit with us.
I am happy to be here.
You did your part. Now eat with us.
I knew that line. I said it with you.
Not all of it. Just that part.

title: The same forecourt
purpose: Introduce farewell meanings in context, never first in a check.
staging: Reuse airport exterior. Player end-game outfit; cousin casual. Driver indicates departure direction.
arc: Departure remains bittersweet; growth is a small capacity to continue.
exchanges: Here we are again. Are you ready?
Would you like water before you go?
Thank you for being with us.
I give thanks to my family.
You are leaving. Goodbye. Travel safely.
We will stay here. Say goodbye to us.
You go. We stay. Goodbye to those staying.

title: One line next time
purpose: Complete the cousin arc without promising fluency or adding messaging systems.
staging: Cousin steps forward; phone remains a prop, no account or actual messaging integration.
arc: Cousin asks to continue the relationship and volunteers one greeting next time.
exchanges: Message me when you get home.
Next time, let me say hello first.

title: A way to return
purpose: Final farewell retrieval and boarding.
staging: Driver waits by transport exit; elder and cousin remain on forecourt. End card after response, no proficiency badge.
arc: Player leaves with a relationship and a usable sentence, not a completed identity.
exchanges: They are staying. You are leaving.
You are leaving. They are staying.

title: Carrying the thanks
purpose: Introduce a role-specific rehearsal fragment; linguistic emphasis differs without extra quests.
staging: Reuse current area edge; no sacred or ceremonial performance at church or sports ground. Relative or cousin speaks privately.
arc: Sione works on speaking without rushing.
exchanges: You will give a short speech. Not a long one.
I want to thank them properly.
You can ask to try again.

title: Order matters
purpose: Introduce a role-specific rehearsal fragment; linguistic emphasis differs without extra quests.
staging: Reuse current area edge; no sacred or ceremonial performance at church or sports ground. Relative or cousin speaks privately.
arc: Sione works on speaking without rushing.
exchanges: There is an order to the acknowledgements. We will use the order our elder gives us.
You can ask to try again.

title: A small audience
purpose: Introduce a role-specific rehearsal fragment; linguistic emphasis differs without extra quests.
staging: Reuse current area edge; no sacred or ceremonial performance at church or sports ground. Relative or cousin speaks privately.
arc: Sione works on speaking without rushing.
exchanges: You can practise with me. I will not interrupt.
You can ask to try again.

title: A part in the celebration
purpose: Introduce a role-specific rehearsal fragment; linguistic emphasis differs without extra quests.
staging: Reuse current area edge; no sacred or ceremonial performance at church or sports ground. Relative or cousin speaks privately.
arc: Mele asks what a movement means instead of copying its surface.
exchanges: You will dance. We will practise each movement and what it means.
You can ask to try again.

title: Meaning before memory
purpose: Introduce a role-specific rehearsal fragment; linguistic emphasis differs without extra quests.
staging: Reuse current area edge; no sacred or ceremonial performance at church or sports ground. Relative or cousin speaks privately.
arc: Mele asks what a movement means instead of copying its surface.
exchanges: We will use the movements our elder teaches. Do not guess at their meaning.
You can ask to try again.

title: Someone to practise beside
purpose: Introduce a role-specific rehearsal fragment; linguistic emphasis differs without extra quests.
staging: Reuse current area edge; no sacred or ceremonial performance at church or sports ground. Relative or cousin speaks privately.
arc: Mele asks what a movement means instead of copying its surface.
exchanges: You can practise here. I can watch if you want.
You can ask to try again.

title: The whole contribution, slowly
purpose: Retrieve every previously introduced approval slot, then opening thanks.
staging: Same family room; relative models on request.
arc: Player uses help without surrendering the contribution.

title: The microphone
purpose: Apply practised order.
staging: Microphone and elder reactions.
arc: Player can recover in the same room.

title: The whole contribution, slowly
purpose: Retrieve every previously introduced approval slot, then opening thanks.
staging: Same family room; relative models on request.
arc: Player uses help without surrendering the contribution.

title: The first movement
purpose: Apply practised movement/meaning pairs.
staging: Four preplaced guest sprites; provisional threshold three.
arc: Player can recover in the same room.
